evidence.description: The 'items' set is modified on a background thread (within the dataTask completion handler) without synchronization.

candidates.explanation: The 'items' property is a 'Set' which is not thread-safe. It is being mutated inside a 'dataTask' completion handler, which executes on a background thread, while other methods like 'load' access it on the caller's thread.
candidates.title: Thread-safety violation

evidence.description: The 'subscriptions' property is declared as public but is not initialized in the initializer, leading to it being an empty array that is never populated by the provided methods.

candidates.explanation: The 'subscriptions' property is marked 'public' but is never assigned to or utilized within the class, suggesting it may be an incomplete implementation or an unnecessary public API.
candidates.title: Unused public property

evidence.description: The 'load' method uses 'items.first(where:)' which is an O(n) operation on a collection that could grow large.

candidates.explanation: The code performs a linear search on a 'Set' to find an item by URL. Since 'Set' is intended for O(1) lookups, using 'first(where:)' defeats the performance benefits of the collection type.
candidates.title: Inefficient lookup

evidence.description: The 'load' method initiates a 'download' but does not provide a mechanism to handle the asynchronous nature of the result or notify the subscriber of the completion.

candidates.explanation: When an item is not found in the local cache, 'download(url)' is called. However, the 'load' method returns immediately after calling 'download', and there is no visible mechanism in the 'Publisher' interface provided to deliver the eventual result to the 'subscriber' passed in 'load'.
candidates.title: Inconsistent asynchronous handling

evidence.description: The 'Item' struct implements 'Hashable' and 'Equatable' manually but only uses the 'url' property for equality and hashing.

candidates.explanation: The 'Item' struct contains both 'url' and 'data' properties, but only 'url' is used for 'hash(into:)' and '=='. This can lead to issues where two different items with the same URL but different data are treated as identical in a 'Set'.
candidates.title: Incomplete Hashable implementation
